newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends up on weather concerns, fund buying.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends up on weather concerns, fund buying.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed sharply higher on fund buying amid concerns about forecasts for hotter and drier weather in the U.S. Midwest and on the lack of improvement in U.S. corn condition ratings last week, traders said.
New crop December corn on July 7 fell to its contract low of $2.27-1/2 a bushel based on market assumptions for excellent crop weather through the summer in the U.S. Midwest.

"I think the market had broken too far basically on perfect weather conditions, it had broken to a weather discount," said Charlie Sernatinger, analyst for E.D. and F. Man International. Now "we may see one to 1-1/2 more sessions of technical (fund) buying. The technical objectives are $2.73 for Dec corn and $6.62-1/2 for November beans."
December corn Tuesday ended 8-1/4 cents higher at $2.60-1/4 a bushel and November soybeans closed up 17-1/4 cents at $6.36-1/2.
Fund buying Tuesday totalled at least 30 million bushels and probably was closer to 50 million bushels, traders said. Griffin Trading bought 10.0 million bushels of December.
Corn futures closed 2-3/4 to 8-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with September up 7-1/2 at $2.58 a bushel.

USDA Monday said the U.S. corn crop as of Sunday was 68 percent good to excellent, the same as in that category a week ago. The market was expecting at least a mild improvement in the condition rating for the U.S. corn crop.

Also USDA Monday said 60 percent of the corn crop was silking (pollinating) as of Sunday, ahead of 45 percent a year ago as well as the 55 percent average pollination pace. Corn that is pollinating would benefit from warm and humid weather not hot and dry conditions.
U.S. meteorologists see cooler temperatures and clear skies for much of the Midwest in the next two days followed by hotter weather and a chance for scattered rains by the end of the week.
Central Illinois and Indiana, which are the areas considered most in need of rain, are unlikely to receive much precipitation until next week, forecasters said.

Traders also said the latest National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook was supportive for corn futures. NWS Monday said from August 3 through August 7 in the U.S. Midwest temperatures would be normal to above normal and rainfall would be mostly normal to below normal in key western Corn Belt areas and above normal in the eastern growing region.
The market also was paying closer attention to reports of dry weather in portions of China's grain growing region.
Rand Financial bought seven million bushels of December, Refco Inc bought six million December and R.J. O'Brien bought four million December, traders said.
Term Commodities sold eight million bushels of December, ADM Investor Services sold three million December and LIT America bought two million December but sold five million December, traders said.
In spread dealings, Continental Grain did five million bushels of September/December at 1-1/2 cents, premium December, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 80,000 contracts, above the 61,125 traded Monday.

In corn options, Farmers Commodities Corp bought 2,000 September $2.30 puts, sold 1,000 September $2.20 puts and sold 1,000 September $2.40 puts at 7/8 cent, floor sources said. Refco Inc bought 1,200 December $2.60 calls, sold 1,200 December $2.80 calls and sold 1,200 December $2.40 puts at a 3/4 cent debit to 1/2 cent credit, sources said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, above the 18,790 traded Monday.
